region: Villabuena de Álava · Rioja Alavesa, Spain
about: Bideona is a young name built on old vines. In 2018 Basque txakoli producer Gorka Izagirre bought an existing winery in Villabuena de Álava, in Rioja Alavesa, the smallest and northernmost of Rioja’s three subregions. Winemaking and management were handed to Península Viticultores, the company of Masters of Wine Sam Harrop and Andreas Kubach, who describe their aim as making “wines of place instead of wines of style.” The first vintage was made in a temporary tented cellar; a new winery has since been built.

Cabezadas is the entry point to Bideona’s Burgundy-style range, which climbs from regional wines through village wines to single vineyards. The name refers to the cabezada, the upper part of a hillside vineyard, where the grapes for this Viura are grown. Fruit comes from a patchwork of some 300 small parcels, averaging about 0.3 hectares, on limestone and clay terraces below the Sierra de Cantabria, with vines averaging more than 50 years old. The grapes are picked by hand and fermented in a mix of stainless steel, concrete and old oak barriques, partly with native yeasts, and rest only briefly before bottling.

Viura, also called Macabeo, is the traditional white grape of Rioja, long used for oak-aged whites; Bideona takes a lighter path and lets the vineyard speak. The point of the wine is freshness rather than oak. Expect pure stone fruit, a touch of white flowers and a faint struck-match note, then a light, crisp palate and a dry, slightly mineral finish, the cool, high limestone sites of Alavesa showing through in an easy, food-friendly white.
facts: About 300 hillside parcels in Rioja Alavesa; vines average 50+ years
Stainless steel, concrete and old oak barriques; native and house-cultured yeasts
Brief rest in the fermentation vessels; no significant new oak
